body:
If you want to do something before rendering has started (maybe in preparation for rendering starting), but after proper frame synchronization has started (ie `xrWaitFrame()`, `xrBeginFrame()`, `xrEndFrame()`), then you'd want to do that in the "sychronized" state. The "ready" state would be too early (because frame synchronization hasn't started yet) and the "visible" state would be too late (because rendering has already begun).

I don't have a concrete example, though, of what that might be.

And it's also possible that this state could be extremely short if the runtime doesn't do anything to show visible transition to the user between apps. Like, some runtimes could animate the old app out and the new app in, so this state will last for a few seconds, but some runtimes may do nothing at all and just jump right to rendering so this state only lasts 1ms.

But I think it makes sense for the developer to be informed of this transition in case there is something they do want to do there.

Please use [Oxford comma](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/documentation/docs_writing_guidelines.html#use-the-oxford-comma-to-enumerate-anything).

In this case, maybe we should just remove the "OpenXR*" prefix entirely?

This is an enum inside of `OpenXRInterface`, so, we could just call it `SessionState`? It would be addressed as `OpenXRInterface.SessionState` - we don't need to say "OpenXR" twice.

However, I do feel pretty strongly that we shouldn't start naming types as `OpenXr` with a lower-case `r`, because it'll be super weird to have some types as `OpenXR*` (which is everything currently merged), and some as `OpenXr*`. Autocomplete will help, but I think this will create confusion.

I'm happy to change this (and spatial entities enums) to have a capital R, I'm not going to die on the hill just for the pascal case issue. C# devs will just have to deal with that :P
